figures.finding: No collective agreement or statutory rule sets a Thai actor's pay or hours: in July 2026 the Labour Ministry said film and entertainment workers commonly take jobs without written contracts, are not paid as agreed and work more than 16 consecutive hours, and it set up a working group with the Thai Film Directors Association and the Association of Thai Actors to study working-hour standards for film crews.

value.status: Labour Ministry working group studying working-hour standards (July 2026)

figures.applies: Thailand, film and entertainment workers, as of 5 July 2026.

sources.said: She said common problems included excessively long working hours, accepting jobs without written contracts, not being paid as agreed, and lacking proper job security and welfare benefits.

The Labour Ministry is working with the Thai Film Directors Association, the Association of Thai Actors and the wider creative media industry to raise employment and labour protection standards across the sector.

the Labour Ministry is preparing to set up a joint working group with representatives from the industry to study whether formal working-hour standards should be introduced for film crew members. The move follows concerns that some production workers are still required to work more than 16 consecutive hours a day

figures.finding: Bangkok hosted 325 of the 491 foreign productions filmed in Thailand in 2024 (Pathum Thani 85, Chon Buri 68, Phuket 37), by the Thailand Film Office's report; Thai productions' locations are not counted.
